candidates.title: MEMORY VOLLEY
candidates.description: Targets flash a short order at each round's start; tap them back in that exact order for a chain bonus, but tapping out of order breaks the streak and only pops a single target.

candidates.title: SLICE VECTOR
candidates.description: Drag a straight cut through the field to slice every target it crosses, spending a slowly-regenerating stamina meter proportional to the cut's length.

candidates.title: ARC LAUNCHER
candidates.description: Drag back and release to fling a projectile along a physics arc, where pull distance sets power and pull angle sets the launch trajectory toward distant targets.

candidates.title: CORE OVERLOAD
candidates.description: Three reactor nodes build heat on their own; hold on a node to vent its heat into score, chasing a full-drain bonus while racing to keep the other nodes from overflowing.

candidates.title: CHAIN IGNITE
candidates.description: Tap a target to ignite it and pass the ignition along its faint connecting lines to linked targets after a short delay, but tapping one still on cooldown fizzles the whole chain.

candidates.title: MIRROR STEER
candidates.description: Drag continuously rotates a central mirror to deflect a steady stream of incoming projectiles into color-matched goal slots at the screen's edges.

candidates.title: TRIAGE PULSE
candidates.description: Several targets appear at once, each with its own shrinking value ring, but only one tap is allowed per short cooldown, forcing a choice of which to take before it bottoms out.

candidates.title: LOOP LASSO
candidates.description: Drag a closed loop around clusters of drifting orbs; only orbs fully enclosed when the loop closes are captured, and loop length draws from a slowly-regenerating stamina budget.

candidates.title: SPLIT AIM DUO
candidates.description: Drag steers a pair of reticles that move in mirrored symmetry across the center, requiring one drag path to align both on two separate targets at once.

reason: CORE OVERLOAD scored highest overall (26 vs 25 and 25), tying for the top C1/C6 marks and leading outright on C4 and C7: choosing which of three simultaneously rising nodes to vent before it overflows is a concurrent-attention decision none of the 12 existing works have, it pays off visibly on every hold, and it keeps demanding faster switching as heat rates escalate — and its large fixed hold-zone interaction is also the most stably implementable and testable of the three finalists.
